title: CloudIR-Bench: A Benchmark for Root Cause Analysis and Mitigation of Cloud Incidents
title_zh: CloudIR-Bench：用于云事件根因分析与缓解的基准测试

paragraphs.en: Root cause analysis (RCA) and mitigation prediction are essential for incident management, enabling the identification of underlying causes of failures and ensuring the reliability of complex cloud-based systems. With rising incident volume and system complexity, incident reports have become a valuable resource for these tasks. Recent studies have shown promising results using Large Language Models (LLMs) to predict root causes and mitigation actions from textual descriptions in incident reports. Despite these advances, further progress is hindered by the lack of publicly available datasets; existing work relies on private data, which limits transparency, reproducibility, and generalization. To address this gap, we introduce CloudIR-Bench, the first publicly available benchmark providing a dataset and evaluation framework for incident report-based RCA and mitigation prediction. Curated from incident reports across five leading cloud-based systems, CloudIR-Bench captures a diverse range of real-world production scenarios representing authentic failures and engineers’ reasoning. We also release an open-source evaluation framework that includes eight recent LLM-based approaches. Our comprehensive evaluation includes zero-shot and in-context learning experiments, along with a qualitative analysis to identify where and why LLMs fail. Benchmarking results reveal the capabilities and limitations of existing LLMs in this domain. The benchmark, including the dataset, framework and supplementary materials, is available at https://github.com/hoangtnm/CloudIR-Bench .

Over the past decade, advances in cloud computing technologies have driven a widespread migration of software systems from on-premises servers to cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. Despite significant investments in cloud system reliability [ 1 , 34 , 5 , 9 ] , unplanned incidents (e.g., service failures, unexpected disruptions, and performance degradations) remain unavoidable. These incidents can severely impact organizational profitability and customer satisfaction. For example, a single hour of downtime during peak sales costs Amazon up to $100 million in revenue loss [ 29 ] .

When an incident occurs, it is essential to quickly identify the root cause and propose an effective mitigation strategy to minimize operational and financial impact. As such, root cause analysis (RCA) and mitigation prediction have become crucial to ensure the reliability of modern cloud-based systems. While traditional RCA research primarily leverages telemetry data (logs, metrics, and traces) [ 21 , 36 , 32 , 23 ] , recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled a new research direction: performing RCA directly from unstructured incident reports [ 1 , 5 , 34 , 9 , 27 , 26 ] . These reports capture rich contextual information, including service interactions, human-level reasoning, and customer impacts, which are often invisible in raw telemetry data. Consequently, incident reports have become a key resource for effective RCA and mitigation planning, supporting both rapid incident response and long-term system reliability. For example, the work in [ 1 ] was the first to leverage LLMs trained on a private historical dataset of incident reports, where each report includes details on incident symptoms, root causes, and mitigation strategies, to identify root causes and mitigation plans for new incidents. The work in [ 34 ] proposed an in-context learning approach enabling LLMs to learn effectively from historical incident reports and improve RCA and mitigation prediction for new incidents. Furthermore, the work in [ 16 ] demonstrates that fine-tuning language models on incident ticket titles and descriptions can achieve highly accurate multi-class classification of incident tickets, complementing free-text root cause prediction by enabling rapid incident triage and automated routing to appropriate resolution teams in production systems.
Despite the promising results of LLM-based approaches for incident report-based RCA reported in these studies, this research direction still faces significant challenges:

Lack of public datasets: Existing work relies exclusively on private data, which is not publicly shared due to confidentiality and privacy constraints. This lack of accessibility limits reproducibility, hinders standardized evaluation, and impedes broader research progress. Currently, there is no publicly available dataset or benchmark for RCA and mitigation prediction based on incident reports.

Challenges in dataset construction: Building a well-curated dataset of incident reports is technically challenging. Incident reports often vary significantly in format and language, requiring extensive preprocessing. Moreover, extracting root causes and mitigation actions typically requires manual expert annotation, as such information is often implicit or loosely defined within each report.

To address these challenges and advance research on incident report-based RCA and mitigation prediction, we introduce CloudIR-Bench , the first publicly available benchmark that includes both a dataset and an evaluation framework for these tasks in cloud-based systems. Our dataset contains incident reports curated from five leading cloud-based systems, covering a wide range of real-world production incidents, including configuration errors, software/hardware failures, network issues, cascading failures, and service dependency failures. These reports were originally documented by the engineers responsible for handling the incidents, and we extract the detailed incident information, along with the corresponding root causes and mitigation actions as ground-truth labels for the RCA and mitigation prediction tasks. Specifically, each dataset entry contains the title, summary, impact, timeline, along with the corresponding root cause and mitigation plans, all presented in free-form text. As such, CloudIR-Bench serves as a rich textual resource for AI-driven RCA and mitigation prediction, supporting not only these key tasks, but also related tasks such as information retrieval and processing of unstructured incident reports. For evaluation, CloudIR-Bench includes an open-source framework that provides a unified experimental environment for evaluating recent LLMs in RCA and mitigation prediction. The framework leverages standard APIs for LLM inference, simplifying integration and enabling seamless model interchangeability. We further evaluate recent LLMs to reveal key insights into their capabilities for identifying root causes and predicting mitigation plans from incident reports, motivating further research in this area.
In summary, our key contributions are as follows:

The first public incident report dataset : We introduce CloudIR-Bench, the first publicly available dataset of incident reports curated from five leading cloud-based systems. The dataset is enriched with long-context information and metadata to support a deep understanding of incident diagnosis and mitigation. It is constructed following established best practices to ensure data quality and promote transparency in RCA and mitigation prediction research. It is also highly diverse, representing a wide range of incident characteristics.

An evaluation framework for incident report-based RCA and mitigation prediction : CloudIR-Bench includes an open-source evaluation framework that enables fair comparisons of recent LLM baselines for incident report–based RCA and mitigation prediction using standard APIs for LLM inference.

A comprehensive evaluation of recent LLMs : Using the proposed dataset and evaluation framework, we conduct an extensive evaluation and analysis of recent LLMs on RCA and mitigation prediction, providing critical insights into the LLMs’ capabilities and limitations.

Production incidents remain a persistent challenge in large-scale cloud-based systems, negatively affecting customer satisfaction and requiring substantial costs for RCA and mitigation efforts. A standard incident lifecycle typically includes four stages: (1) Detection, which involves the identification of anomalous system behaviors, through automated monitoring services and customer reports [ 11 , 18 ] ; (2) Triaging, which involves engineers to assess the severity of reported anomalies and assign them to the appropriate team for initial investigation [ 25 , 3 ] ; (3) Diagnosis, during which assigned teams engage in iterative communication and analysis to determine the nature of the incident and identify its root cause [ 17 , 3 ] ; (4) Mitigation, where engineers conduct mitigation strategies based on the identified root cause to resolve the issue and restore the system to normal operation [ 1 , 14 ] .

RCA and mitigation prediction are critical stages of incident management, enabling engineers to identify the underlying causes of failures, implement effective mitigation strategies, and prevent future recurrence [ 6 ] . However, performing RCA and mitigation prediction in cloud environments is complex and resource-intensive, requiring not only expert knowledge but also the ability to interpret heterogeneous and unstructured system data [ 17 ] . As a result, these processes are not only time-consuming but also error-prone, further complicating the incident management process.

Traditional RCA research primarily relies on telemetry-based approaches using logs, metrics, and traces [ 22 , 11 , 8 , 35 ] . While effective for localized fault detection, these approaches often fail to capture full incident context, including service interactions, human reasoning, and customer impacts, which are essential for understanding complex failures.

Our work instead focuses on incident report-based RCA, which is a recent and increasingly important research direction. Given unstructured textual descriptions of incident reports, the goal is to generate the root cause and recommend mitigation strategies in free-form text [ 1 , 34 , 5 , 14 ] . Incident reports, written by engineers during and after incident resolution, capture rich contextual information including system behaviors, cross-service dependencies, human observations, and mitigation actions often invisible in telemetry data. This represents a fundamentally different input modality and research problem from telemetry-based RCA. By analyzing historical incident reports, engineers can gain a deeper understanding of the incident lifecycle, service interactions, and effective mitigation strategies. Moreover, historical incident reports reveal recurring patterns, support predictive modeling, and provide valuable training data for automated RCA and mitigation prediction. For example, BugFixer [ 12 ] and DeepRmd [ 14 ] demonstrate the feasibility of recommending responsible engineers or retrieving relevant troubleshooting documents that describe mitigation processes from historical incident reports.

Recently, the lifecycle of incident management has been transformed by the adoption of LLMs [ 1 , 5 , 34 , 27 ] to enable more sophisticated RCA and mitigation prediction from historical incident reports. [ 1 ] [ 1 ] was the first to apply fine-tuned LLMs, specifically GPT-3.x variants, to cloud incident reports to assist engineers in RCA and mitigation prediction. Fine-tuned on a private dataset of incidents within Microsoft, the study compared multiple training settings and evaluated outputs using both semantic and lexical metrics. The results demonstrated that LLMs can accurately identify the underlying root causes and predict mitigation actions, even in cases where such information is challenging for human experts to identify. Building on this work, subsequent research has proposed to apply advanced prompting strategies, including in-context learning (ICL) and chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, to further improve performance on RCA and mitigation prediction from incident reports [ 34 , 5 , 26 , 9 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 近年来，事件管理的生命周期已因采用大语言模型（LLMs）[ 1 , 5 , 34 , 27 ]而发生变革，使其能够基于历史事件报告实现更复杂的根本原因分析（RCA）与缓解措施预测。[ 1 ] [ 1 ]率先将经过微调的 LLMs（特别是 GPT-3.x 变体）应用于云端事件报告，以协助工程师进行 RCA 和缓解措施预测。该研究在微软内部事件的私有数据集上进行了微调，比较了多种训练设置，并使用语义和词汇两类指标对输出进行了评估。结果表明，LLMs 能够准确识别潜在的根本原因并预测缓解措施，即使在这些信息对人类专家而言难以识别的情况下也是如此。在这一工作基础上，后续研究提出采用先进的提示策略，包括上下文学习（ICL）和思维链（CoT）推理，以进一步提升基于事件报告进行 RCA 和缓解措施预测的性能 [ 34 , 5 , 26 , 9 ] 。

paragraphs.en: It is also worth noting that, in general text generation tasks, a notable performance gap exists between closed-source commercial models (e.g., GPT-5.2, GPT-4.1) and open-weight alternatives such as Llama 3 [ 7 ] , Mixtral [ 13 ] , and DeepSeek-R1 [ 10 ] . Understanding how this performance gap affects the RCA and mitigation prediction tasks remains unknown.

paragraphs.en: Despite the demonstrated success of LLMs for RCA and mitigation prediction, progress in incident report-based RCA research is hindered by the lack of publicly available datasets, as existing datasets are private [ 1 ] , limiting reproducibility and transparency. While telemetry-based RCA datasets (e.g., LEMMA-RCA [ 37 ] , OpenRCA [ 30 ] , RCAEval [ 24 ] ) exist, they address a fundamentally different problem from incident report-based RCA. These telemetry-based benchmarks cannot be adapted for incident report analysis as they lack the unstructured textual context, human reasoning, and cross-service insights captured in engineer-written incident reports.

paragraphs.en: Recognizing the critical need for a public benchmark to advance incident report-based RCA and mitigation prediction research, this work introduces the first publicly available dataset of authentic production incident reports. Our dataset includes diverse types of incident reports from five leading cloud-based systems, capturing real-world engineer reasoning, broader contextual information, and realistic RCA challenges. Additionally, we develop an open-source evaluation framework that enables fair comparisons of recent LLM baselines for incident report–based RCA and mitigation prediction using standard APIs for LLM inference. Finally, we conduct a comprehensive analysis of recent LLMs to provide insights into their current capabilities and limitations in RCA and mitigation prediction in cloud incidents.

paragraphs.en: Guided by the aforementioned criteria, we identified nine cloud-based systems as potential candidates for inclusion in the dataset: Microsoft Azure [ azure ] , Google Cloud [ google_cloud ] , Google Workspace [ google_workspace ] , Atlassian [ atlassian ] , AWS [ aws ] , GitHub [ github ] , CircleCI [ circleci ] , Notion [ notion ] , and Alibaba Cloud [ alibaba_cloud ] . These systems publish post-incident reviews, documented by the engineers in charge, that provide detailed descriptions of incidents after resolution, including incident summaries, root causes, mitigation plans, and other relevant information. Note that, for the incident summaries, our goal is to construct a dataset of incident reports based on the information available at the time of initial incident reporting, so from the post-incident summaries, we keep only the details presented during the initial incident reporting.

sents.en: Note that, for the incident summaries, our goal is to construct a dataset of incident reports based on the information available at the time of initial incident reporting, so from the post-incident summaries, we keep only the details presented during the initial incident reporting.
sents.zh: 需要注意的是，对于事件摘要，我们的目标是基于事件初次上报时的可用信息构建事件报告数据集，因此从事后摘要中，我们仅保留事件初次上报时呈现的细节。

paragraphs.en: We then conducted multiple rounds of manual review for each candidate system, carefully examining their incident reports to assess whether they include detailed incident summaries, root causes, and mitigation steps. During this process, CircleCI, Notion, and Alibaba Cloud were excluded due to the lack of sufficient detail in root cause and mitigation descriptions in most of their incident reports. Among the remaining six systems, AWS was also excluded because it provided a limited number of incident reports (only 17), despite its high quality and thorough documentation.

paragraphs.en: Finally, we selected five cloud-based systems, including Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Google Workspace, Atlassian, and GitHub, to construct the dataset, ensuring both depth and breadth of incident coverage across diverse operational contexts. paragraphs.en: The first step involves crawling raw incident reports from each target data source. Since none of these sources provides official APIs for automated data collection, we employed web scraping techniques as an alternative. Specifically, we developed custom web crawling techniques using Selenium and Beautiful Soup to extract the required information. By parsing and navigating the HTML layouts, we ensure robust and precise data extraction. To accommodate the distinct layouts of each platform, we implemented separate scraping scripts, each tailored to the unique HTML structure of its respective data source. The resulting implementation comprises approximately 1,500 lines of code, enabling us to unify the extracted data into a standardized and consistent JSON format.

paragraphs.en: Our analysis of the collected data from the five selected cloud-based systems reveals that a substantial portion of the raw incident reports lacks meaningful content and includes duplicate incident reports. Specifically, in many cases, the reports consist of only brief summaries stating that the issue has been resolved while omitting critical information such as the root cause or mitigation steps. As a result, these reports offer limited value for the dataset. To address this issue, we first removed duplicates and kept only reports with substantive information such as title, summary, root cause, and mitigation steps (Section III-D1 ). We then excluded any reports that lack either the root cause or mitigation steps, as they do not provide useful insights (Section III-D2 ). Furthermore, since each organization uses a distinct format for documenting incidents, we develop customized filtering and extraction strategies for each system to ensure consistent and relevant information is extracted from the incident reports (Section III-D3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 我们对五个选定基于云的系统的收集数据分析后发现，很大一部分原始事故报告缺乏有意义的内容，并且包含重复的事故报告。 具体而言，在许多情况下，这些报告仅包含简短的摘要，声称问题已经解决，却省略了关键信息，例如根本原因或缓解步骤。 因此，这些报告对数据集的价值有限。 为解决这一问题，我们首先去除了重复报告，仅保留包含实质性信息的报告，例如标题、摘要、根本原因和缓解步骤（第 III-D1 节）。 随后，我们排除了任何缺少根本原因或缓解步骤的报告，因为它们无法提供有用的洞见（第 III-D2 节）。 此外，由于每个组织使用不同的格式记录事故，我们为每个系统开发了定制化的过滤和提取策略，以确保从事故报告中提取一致且相关的信息（第 III-D3 节）。

paragraphs.en: In large-scale cloud-based systems, many services and components are often tightly interconnected. As a result, a single underlying fault can propagate across multiple services, leading to simultaneous failures and causing the same incident to be reported multiple times across different services/components. This necessitates a de-duplication process to ensure the uniqueness of incident reports. Since each system employs different mechanisms for tracking and documenting incidents, we design tailored de-duplication strategies for each system to accurately identify and remove redundant ones, ensuring each incident is represented only once in the dataset. For example, when multiple incident reports share the same incident ID within a system, we keep only the earliest report and discard the duplicates.
paragraphs.zh: 在大规模云端系统中，许多服务与组件往往紧密互联。 因此，单个底层故障可能在多个服务之间传播，导致同时发生多个故障，并使同一事件在不同服务/组件中被多次上报。 这就需要一个去重过程来确保事件报告的唯一性。 由于每个系统在跟踪和记录事件时采用不同的机制，我们为每个系统设计了定制化的去重策略，以准确识别并删除冗余报告，确保每起事件在数据集中只出现一次。 例如，当同一系统内多份事件报告共享相同的事件 ID 时，我们只保留最早的那份报告并丢弃重复项。

paragraphs.en: In this step, we screen the collected incident reports obtained from the previous step to ensure that the dataset includes only those reports with valid root cause and mitigation information. Moreover, given the large volume of reports in this collection, manually labeling all of them would be inefficient and error-prone. To address this, we first apply an automated keyword-based filtering method using predefined extraction patterns (detailed in Section A2 in the appendix [ appendixlink ] ) to exclude reports that are unlikely to contain relevant root cause or mitigation information, thereby reducing the dataset size. We then manually review the filtered reports to verify their relevance and to minimize the risk of excluding valuable reports.
paragraphs.zh: 在这一步中，我们对上一步收集到的事件报告进行筛选，以确保数据集仅包含那些具有有效根因信息和缓解信息的报告。 此外，鉴于该报告集合数量庞大，人工对所有报告进行标注将效率低下且容易出错。 为解决这一问题，我们首先采用基于关键词的自动化过滤方法，使用预定义的抽取模式（详见附录 A2 节 [ appendixlink ]），以排除不太可能包含相关根因或缓解信息的报告，从而缩减数据集规模。 随后，我们人工审查过滤后的报告，以核实其相关性，并最大限度降低遗漏有价值报告的风险。

paragraphs.en: Label Annotation. We extracted key attributes from each incident report, including Title, Summary, Impact, Root Cause, Mitigation, Updates, Severity, Status, and Timestamp. While structured fields (severity, status, timestamp) can be extracted automatically, most attributes require manual annotation due to their unstructured nature. To preserve the authenticity of the original public reports, we keep the extracted fields in their original form rather than paraphrasing them. Special emphasis is placed on the fields “Summary”, “Root Cause”, and “Mitigation” as they are critical for understanding the system failures, identifying the root causes, and predicting the mitigation strategies. Furthermore, given that our data sources are post-incident reviews, some summaries may include sentences that might reveal root causes or mitigation. We call this “information leakage”. To address this, we identify and remove such information from incident reports, ensuring that root-cause or mitigation information is not accessible to LLMs during evaluation. To reduce bias, each incident report is independently annotated by two authors with software engineering expertise, followed by a consensus verification.
paragraphs.zh: 标签标注。 我们从每份事故报告中提取关键属性，包括标题、摘要、影响、根本原因、缓解措施、更新、严重程度、状态和时间戳。 虽然结构化字段（严重程度、状态、时间戳）可以自动提取，但大多数属性由于其非结构化的性质，需要人工标注。 为了保持原始公开报告的真实性，我们保留提取字段的原有形式，而不对其进行改写。 我们特别强调“摘要”、“根本原因”和“缓解措施”这几个字段，因为它们对于理解系统故障、识别根本原因以及预测缓解策略至关重要。 此外，鉴于我们的数据来源是事后复盘报告，一些摘要中可能包含会泄露根本原因或缓解措施的句子。 我们将这种现象称为“信息泄露”。 为解决这一问题，我们从事故报告中识别并删除此类信息，确保在评估过程中大语言模型无法获取根本原因或缓解措施相关的信息。 为减少偏差，每份事故报告由两位具有软件工程专业知识的作者独立标注，随后进行共识核验。

paragraphs.en: Consensus Verification. Since each report is annotated by two labelers, disagreement may arise. These are resolved through discussion. Furthermore, to understand the inter-annotator agreement across the labelers, we compute the Cohen’s Kappa score κ \kappa . The resulting scores indicate strong overall agreement. Specifically, Summary, Root Cause, and Mitigation achieve κ \kappa of 0.89-0.91 for Azure, Google Cloud, and Google Workspace, and 0.63-0.64 for GitHub and Atlassian, while temporal fields such as Start-time, End-time, and Updates achieve κ \kappa of 0.71-1.00 across all datasets. These results indicate strong agreement among the labelers.

paragraphs.en: CloudIR-Bench covers an extensive range of production failures and fault types across diverse cloud infrastructures, representing real-world scenarios from multiple organizations rather than being restricted to a single company’s internal data. Failure categories include configuration errors, service dependencies, cascading failures, resource exhaustion, software bugs, and infrastructure issues. This multi-organizational scope gives CloudIR-Bench broader fault coverage than single-organization proprietary datasets, making it comparable to or more representative than industry-private alternatives, while remaining publicly accessible for reproducible research.
paragraphs.zh: CloudIR-Bench 涵盖了多样化云基础设施中广泛的生产故障与故障类型，代表来自多个组织的真实场景，而非局限于单一公司的内部数据。 故障类别包括配置错误、服务依赖、级联故障、资源耗尽、软件缺陷以及基础设施问题。 这种多组织的覆盖范围使 CloudIR-Bench 比单一组织的专有数据集具有更广泛的故障覆盖面，使其与行业私有替代方案相当或更具代表性，同时保持公开可访问以支持可复现研究。

paragraphs.en: To evaluate our proposed CloudIR-Bench dataset and understand the current state of LLM-based methods for RCA and mitigation prediction, we provide an open-source evaluation framework alongside the dataset. Our evaluation framework includes 8 LLM baselines, covering a wide range of closed-source and open-weight LLMs, and uses standard APIs for LLM inference. It also supports data preprocessing and benchmarking with both lexical and semantic metrics. Detailed documentation is available on our GitHub repository [ appendixlink ] , including instructions for installation, usage, and steps for integrating other baselines. The documentation also provides example workflows and guidance to ensure reproducibility.

paragraphs.en: To thoroughly assess model performance and understand the underlying factors that affect the prediction quality, we investigate the following research questions (RQs):
paragraphs.zh: 为了全面评估模型性能并理解影响预测质量的潜在因素，我们研究了以下研究问题（RQs）：

paragraphs.en: RQ1: How effective are LLM-based methods in identifying the root causes from incident reports?
paragraphs.zh: RQ1：基于大语言模型的方法在从事故报告中识别根本原因方面效果如何？

paragraphs.en: RQ2: How effective are LLM-based methods in predicting the mitigation plans from incident reports?
paragraphs.zh: RQ2：基于大语言模型（LLM）的方法在从事故报告中预测缓解计划方面的效果如何？

paragraphs.en: RQ3: How effective is In-Context Learning in improving the performance of LLMs?
paragraphs.zh: RQ3：上下文学习（In-Context Learning）在提升大语言模型性能方面的效果如何？

paragraphs.en: RQ4: Where and why do LLMs fail in RCA and mitigation prediction tasks?
paragraphs.zh: RQ4：大语言模型在根因分析（RCA）与缓解措施预测任务中在哪里失败、为什么失败？

paragraphs.en: To evaluate the proposed benchmark dataset and gain insights into LLM-based RCA and mitigation prediction methods, we conduct experiments comparing baseline models from prior work with other recent LLMs. For closed-source models, we select GPT-4.1 and GPT-5.2 as the direct successors to GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 variants used in prior work [ 1 , 34 ] , but are now deprecated. For open-weight models, we select top-ranked and widely adopted LLMs on SWE-bench while covering various model sizes and architectures. Figure 3 illustrates the experimental workflow, outlining key stages including label generation, model inference, and evaluation.

paragraphs.en: The evaluation begins by using the title, summary, and impact of an incident report as input to the LLM-based methods. Since incident reports are often lengthy and contain extensive details, they may introduce noise that obscures the core incident information and complicates downstream inference and evaluation tasks [ 1 , 34 , 5 ] . To address this challenge, following prior works [ 34 , 5 ] , we preprocess each incident report using an LLM-based summarization module, specifically OpenAI’s GPT-4.1, to generate a concise summary that captures the essential information of the report. Since leaked sentences are removed prior to summarization, there is no exposure of root cause or mitigation beyond what was already filtered during annotation. Both the incident title and the summarized summary are then used as inputs to LLMs to predict root causes and mitigation.
paragraphs.zh: 评估首先以事故报告的标题、摘要和影响作为基于大语言模型方法的输入。 由于事故报告通常篇幅较长且包含大量细节，可能引入噪声，掩盖核心事故信息，并使下游推理与评估任务变得复杂 [ 1 , 34 , 5 ] 。 为应对这一挑战，遵循先前的工作 [ 34 , 5 ] ，我们使用基于大语言模型的摘要模块（具体为 OpenAI 的 GPT-4.1）对每份事故报告进行预处理，生成一份能抓住报告关键信息的简明摘要。 由于泄露句子在摘要生成之前已被移除，因此不会暴露超出标注阶段已过滤内容之外的根本原因或缓解措施。 事故标题和生成的摘要随后被用作大语言模型的输入，以预测根本原因和缓解措施。

paragraphs.en: To quantitatively assess model performance on CloudIR-Bench, we compare predictions against the ground-truth root causes and mitigation actions using both lexical and semantic metrics, following established evaluation protocols in prior work [ 1 , 34 , 26 , 27 , 9 , 28 ] . While RCA and mitigation prediction involve semantic reasoning, these metrics capture meaningful signals. Lexical overlap reflects whether key technical terms (e.g., service names, failure types) are correctly identified, while semantic similarity measures whether the predictions have similar meaning even when phrased differently. We do not adopt LLM-as-a-judge in this work due to three limitations: (1) LLMs tend to assign higher scores when used for both prediction and evaluation [ 38 ] ; (2) accurate RCA requires domain-specific knowledge beyond general-purpose LLMs; and (3) non-determinism and prompt sensitivity lead to inconsistent scores across inference runs.

paragraphs.en: Following existing work for RCA [ 1 , 34 , 9 , 26 ] , we employ three standard lexical metrics. We adopt BLEU-4 [ 20 ] , which quantifies n n -gram overlap from unigrams to 4-grams between model predictions and ground-truth labels. We then choose ROUGE-L [ 15 ] to assess sentence-level structural similarity by identifying the longest matching subsequence between the prediction and reference through Longest Common Subsequence (LCS). Lastly, we use METEOR [ 2 ] to evaluate the harmonic mean of unigram precision and recall while incorporating features such as stemming and synonym matching. For RCA and mitigation prediction, a higher score indicates that the prediction shares more technical entities with the label, such as affected services, configuration parameters, suggesting more accurate identification of the incident’s key elements and vice versa.

paragraphs.en: Since root cause and mitigation strategies can be expressed in various ways, lexical metrics that rely on word-level matching may fail to capture the true semantic similarity [ 1 , 34 , 9 , 26 ] . To address this, we perform semantic evaluation alongside lexical evaluation to ensure a more comprehensive assessment that reflects the underlying meaning. Specifically, we employ BERTScore [ 33 ] , a widely used semantic evaluation metric in RCA research [ 1 , 34 , 9 , 26 ] , which uses contextualized embeddings from the pretrained language model BERT to compute similarity scores based on token-level cosine similarity. This approach captures semantic equivalence in linguistics.

paragraphs.en: It’s worth noting that while lexical and semantic metrics are informative and can measure textual overlap or similarity with the ground truth, they do not always capture causal correctness. A prediction can achieve a high similarity score while misidentifying the underlying root cause and actual mitigation steps. We examine this limitation in our qualitative analysis (Section IV-C4 ) and discuss its implications in Section V .

paragraphs.en: Following [ 1 ] , we compute Top1 and Top5 scores for each evaluation metric. For each incident, we generate ten predictions to capture output diversity. The Top1 score is computed by averaging the metric scores of the top-1-ranked prediction (based on the LLM’s confidence scores) across all incidents. The Top5 score is computed by selecting the highest metric score among the top-5-ranked predictions for each incident and averaging these scores across all incidents. Top1 reflects the quality of the model’s most-confident prediction, whereas Top5 reflects the best achievable performance when selecting from the five highest-ranked predictions. Thus, Top5 represents an upper bound on the performance achievable by a downstream selection mechanism (e.g., human review of a shortlist) that can reliably identify the best candidate from the top-5-ranked predictions.
paragraphs.zh: 参照 [ 1 ]，我们为每个评估指标计算 Top1 和 Top5 分数。 对于每个事件，我们生成十个预测以捕捉输出的多样性。 Top1 分数的计算方式是：对所有事件中排名第一的预测（基于大语言模型的置信度分数）的指标分数取平均。 Top5 分数的计算方式是：对每个事件，从前五名的预测中选取最高的指标分数，再对所有事件的这些分数取平均。 Top1 反映模型最有信心的预测的质量，而 Top5 反映从前五名预测中进行选择时可达到的最佳性能。 因此，Top5 代表了一种下游选择机制（例如，对入围名单进行人工审查）所能达到的性能上限，该机制能够可靠地从排名前五的预测中识别出最佳候选。

paragraphs.en: The consistently low BLEU-4@Top1 scores for mitigation reflect the inherent difficulty of the task. Unlike root cause, mitigation requires system-specific reasoning about mitigation actions that are not available from incident symptoms. As illustrated in Fig. 4 , LLMs tend to generate generic actions rather than precise, context-specific steps, resulting in minimal word overlap with ground-truth. These findings reveal a capability gap in current LLMs in accurately predicting mitigation and motivate future work on domain-adapted approaches.
paragraphs.zh: 缓解措施在 BLEU-4@Top1 上持续偏低的分数反映了该任务固有的难度。 与根因不同，缓解需要对缓解措施进行特定于系统的推理，而这些措施无法从事件症状中获得。 如图 4 所示，大语言模型往往生成泛化的措施，而非精确的、结合具体上下文的步骤，导致与标准答案的词汇重叠极少。 这些发现揭示了当前大语言模型在准确预测缓解措施方面的能力差距，并推动了未来对领域自适应方法的研究。

paragraphs.en: To understand the performance of tuned models that learned from historical datasets and how they compare with generic LLMs, we conducted additional experiments using GPT-4.1 and GPT-5.2 with In-Context Learning (ICL). We focus on ICL as it has been shown to improve RCA performance in prior work [ 34 , 5 , 26 , 9 ] and is the most widely adopted strategy in existing studies. Unlike fine-tuning, ICL requires no parameter updates or hyper-param tuning, which is known to be sensitive and costly when labeled data is scarce [ 4 ] , while SOTA LLMs can achieve good performance through well-constructed examples alone [ 19 ] , enabling direct and fair comparison across models. Following established practices [ 34 ] , we allocated 70% of each dataset for ICL examples and 30% for evaluation. For each validation incident, we retrieved the five most relevant incidents from the ICL pool using semantic similarity (with OpenAI’s GPT-OSS). Table IV presents the comparison between zero-shot and ICL settings of these models across the datasets.
paragraphs.zh: 为了理解从历史数据集中学习得到的调优模型的性能，以及它们与通用大语言模型（LLM）相比的表现，我们使用 GPT-4.1 和 GPT-5.2 结合上下文学习（ICL）进行了额外的实验。 我们聚焦于 ICL，因为已有研究 [34, 5, 26, 9] 表明它能提升根因分析（RCA）性能，并且它是现有研究中最广泛采用的策略。 与微调不同，ICL 不需要参数更新或超参数调优——在标注数据稀缺时，这些工作已知是敏感且代价高昂的 [4]——而 SOTA 大语言模型仅通过精心构建的示例就能取得良好性能 [19]，从而实现跨模型的直接、公平比较。 遵循已有实践 [34]，我们将每个数据集的 70% 用作 ICL 示例，30% 用于评估。 对于每个验证事件，我们使用语义相似度（借助 OpenAI 的 GPT-OSS）从 ICL 池中检索出五个最相关的事件。 表 IV 展示了这些模型在各数据集上零样本设置与 ICL 设置之间的比较。

paragraphs.en: RCA Insights. ICL yields consistent but modest improvements in semantic similarity across all datasets, while its effect on lexical overlap remains inconsistent. For GPT-4.1, Azure exhibits the clearest gains, especially in BLEU-4@Top1, METEOR@Top1, and BERTScore@Top1. In contrast, Google Cloud and GitHub show divergent behavior between semantic and lexical metrics: BERTScore@Top1 improves marginally on both Google Cloud and GitHub, but BLEU-4@Top1 collapses to 0 in both cases. Google Workspace and Atlassian, meanwhile, achieve the strongest absolute performance under ICL. Taken together, these results indicate that ICL reliably strengthens semantic alignment with the ground truth across all datasets, but its benefit is dataset-dependent.
paragraphs.zh: RCA 洞察。 ICL 在所有数据集上都带来了稳定但幅度不大的语义相似度提升，而它对词汇重合度的影响则不一致。 对于 GPT-4.1，Azure 表现出最明显的提升，尤其是在 BLEU-4@Top1、METEOR@Top1 和 BERTScore@Top1 上。 相比之下，Google Cloud 和 GitHub 在语义指标与词汇指标上表现出分歧：BERTScore@Top1 在 Google Cloud 和 GitHub 上均有小幅提升，但 BLEU-4@Top1 在两种情况下都骤降为 0。 与此同时，Google Workspace 和 Atlassian 在 ICL 下取得了最强的绝对性能。 综合来看，这些结果表明 ICL 在所有数据集上都能可靠地增强与真实答案的语义对齐，但其收益依赖于具体数据集。

For GPT-4.1, Azure improves in ROUGE-L@Top1 and BERTScore@Top1, while Google Cloud shows a similar improvement in METEOR@Top1, even though BLEU-4@Top1 again drops to 0. GitHub sees the biggest improvement overall, especially in BLEU-4@Top1 and BERTScore@Top1, showing ICL works especially well for this dataset. paragraphs.en: Classification Scheme. For each prediction-reference pair, annotators assessed semantic alignment with the reference, then classified each prediction into a category reflecting its correctness or error type [ 26 ] . Correct predictions were classified as: (1) Precise (precisely matching the reference), (2) Imprecise (semantically matching but missing details), or (3) Hallucination (semantically correct but containing factual errors). Incorrect predictions were classified as: (1) Hallucination (factual errors in content), (2) Reasoning Error (logical errors in reasoning), (3) Insufficient Evidence (refraining from making a prediction), or (4) Other (unknown error). This taxonomy enables the identification of failure modes and ensures a context-aware assessment of predictions.

paragraphs.en: RCA Insights. LLMs achieve modest RCA correctness (26.4%). While correct predictions are often semantically aligned, they often lack technical precision. Errors are dominated by hallucinations and faulty reasoning, where LLMs predict plausible but incorrect information or misinfer causal chains. Model-specific patterns show trade-offs: Qwen3-32B shows the highest reasoning error rate, likely from its reasoning chain, whereas DeepSeek-R1 balances both error types. GPT-4.1 leans toward hallucinations, suggesting overconfident pattern generation misaligned with the ground truth. These failures likely stem from limited evidence, plausible-sounding predictions, and over-generalized root causes.

paragraphs.en: Title: Incident affecting Admin Console Summary: The incident report documented a 5 hour and 30-minute period on Monday, 18 July 2022, during which Google Cloud and Google Workspace Support customers were unable to attach files to new and existing support cases via the Cloud Console and Admin Console. This affected 100% of users for both services, with support case creation remaining unaffected. The incident impacted file uploads specifically, while support case creation functionality remained intact. Reference root cause: File upload service became inaccessible due to a configuration change in the Global Service Load Balancer, causing intermittent failures for users uploading files. Reference mitigation: The incident was mitigated by disabling the file attachment feature and rolling back the GSLB configuration change. Predicted root cause: The root cause was a failure in the file upload functionality within the Admin Console, likely due to an issue with the backend service, API, or database handling file uploads, preventing users from successfully attaching files to support cases. Predicted mitigation: The incident was resolved by identifying the root cause, implementing a fix to restore file upload functionality, communicating updates to users, and conducting a post-mortem analysis to improve future response processes

paragraphs.en: Key Findings. Our qualitative analysis shows that current LLMs face fundamental challenges in incident report-based RCA and mitigation prediction, with most errors stemming from hallucinations and reasoning failures due to contextual sparsity and limited external evidence. While models can capture high-level patterns, they often omit critical technical details, rely on generic or vague language, fabricate plausible-sounding causes, and repeat surface-level details from the input (see Fig. 4 ). In this case, the model correctly identifies the affected component (file upload) but incorrectly attributes the root cause to a generic “backend service, API, or database” issue rather than the actual configuration change in the Global Service Load Balancer. Despite this error, the prediction still receives high scores for two reasons. First, BLEU-4 and ROUGE-L reward high-frequency terms shared between prediction and ground truth, such as “file upload,” “users”, and phrases like “The incident was mitigated/resolved by” regardless of causal correctness. Second, root cause descriptions often follow an ”A due to B” pattern, where A represents the observed consequence, and B represents the underlying root cause. Models tend to reproduce A, which is usually mentioned in the incident summary, while failing to identify B. Thus, predictions that accurately describe the observed consequences but misidentify the underlying root causes may still receive high scores, reflecting a limitation of automatic evaluation metrics in reasoning-intensive tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 关键发现。 我们的定性分析表明，当前大语言模型在基于事件报告的根因分析与缓解措施预测方面面临根本性挑战，其大多数错误源于幻觉以及因上下文信息稀疏和外部证据有限而导致的推理失败。 尽管模型能够捕捉高层次的模式，但它们常常遗漏关键技术细节，使用笼统或模糊的表述，编造听起来合理的成因，并复述输入中的表面细节（见图 4）。 在此案例中，模型正确识别了受影响的组件（文件上传），但错误地将根因归咎于笼统的“后端服务、API 或数据库”问题，而非全局服务负载均衡器中实际发生的配置变更。 尽管存在这一错误，该预测仍然获得了较高的分数，原因有二。 首先，BLEU-4 和 ROUGE-L 会奖励预测与真实标签之间共享的高频词，例如“文件上传”、“用户”，以及诸如“该事件通过……得以缓解/解决”之类的短语，而不考虑因果是否正确。 其次，根因描述通常遵循“A 由于 B”的模式，其中 A 代表观察到的后果，B 代表潜在的根因。 模型倾向于复现 A（通常在事件摘要中已有提及），却未能识别出 B。 因此，那些准确描述了观察到的后果却错误识别了潜在根因的预测，仍可能获得较高的分数，这反映出自动评估指标在推理密集型任务中的局限性。

paragraphs.en: Despite substantial manual effort to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the ground truth annotations, the labeling process is inherently constrained by the lack of direct engagement with the cloud-based system owners. This limitation is mitigated by involving two independent annotators in the labeling process and conducting consensus discussions to resolve discrepancies and agree on the final label for each report. To increase the internal validity of our evaluation, we generate 10 predictions per incident to capture output diversity. We further assess all methods using four metrics and qualitative analysis.

paragraphs.en: Besides, using public post-incident reports introduces specific limitations. Variability and incompleteness are inherent characteristics of real-world incident reports [ 1 ] , rather than a limitation unique to our work, as reports differ in detail, terminology, and technical depth across systems. As a result, ground-truth root causes and mitigation actions reflect what engineers choose to document under operational and disclosure constraints and may not capture all causal factors. Nonetheless, using authentic reports is a practical choice that preserves realism by exposing LLMs to the variability, ambiguity, and incompleteness in real-world scenarios.

paragraphs.en: In this work, we introduce CloudIR-Bench, the first publicly available benchmark for incident report-based RCA and mitigation prediction. CloudIR-Bench addresses a critical gap in the literature by enabling reproducible research in these tasks. It includes a dataset of incident reports curated from five leading cloud-based systems, with each report containing detailed metadata and ground truth labels for root causes and mitigation strategies. In addition, we provide a comprehensive evaluation environment consisting of recent LLM-based methods, further facilitating research in these areas. Finally, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation that highlights both the strengths and limitations of current LLM-based methods in RCA and mitigation prediction. For future work, we plan to explore strategies such as fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agent-based reasoning, and LLM-as-a-judge to advance LLM performance for our benchmark.
paragraphs.zh: 在本工作中，我们提出 CloudIR-Bench，这是首个公开可用的、基于事件报告的根因分析与缓解措施预测基准。 CloudIR-Bench 通过使这些任务的研究具有可复现性，填补了文献中的一项关键空白。 它包含一个从五个领先云系统整理的事件报告数据集，每份报告都含有详细的元数据以及根因和缓解策略的真实标签。 此外，我们还提供了一个由近期基于大语言模型的方法组成的全面评估环境，进一步促进了这些领域的研究。 最后，我们进行了全面评估，突出了当前基于大语言模型的方法在根因分析与缓解措施预测方面的优势与局限。 在未来工作中，我们计划探索微调、检索增强生成（RAG）、基于智能体的推理以及大语言模型作为评判者（LLM-as-a-judge）等策略，以提升大语言模型在该基准上的表现。
